 JEFFERSON COUNTY, Ohio — As colder weather approaches, Ohio Department of Transportation crews are already preparing for the first snow, a process that takes months and starts well before winter arrives.
 ODOT District 11 Public Information Officer Lauren Borell said winter readiness inspections typically begin in September and are conducted statewide to make sure equipment and crews are ready when conditions change.
 "Winter readiness inspections kick off usually in September every year and of course these are conducted in all 88 counties throughout the state," Borell said. "And really, you know, we want to do them. We never know when the snow is going to fly of course, you, know in Ohio, but with those being in September through early November it gives us plenty of time to ensure that everything is ready to go."
 Borell said inspections in District 11 were recently wrapped up.
 "Our inspections were completed last week in all seven of our counties and that includes Belmont, Carroll, Columbiana, Harrison, Holmes, Jefferson, and Tuscarawas," she said.
 Beyond inspections, Borell said preparation includes hands-on training for drivers and employees, including newer staff who may be learning winter operations.
 "You know with newer employees, you know some people might actually see a plow truck out there with the plow on and we're taking them out for training and going over things and just making sure everybody's you know ready for when that snow hits," Borell said.
 Borell also urged drivers to be patient once snow begins falling, noting that ODOT trucks travel below the speed limit and cover long routes that can range from 35 to 40 miles, meaning it can take time for each truck to complete its assigned route.
 "And, of course, our drivers are able to take a break, you know, and they do need those breaks for when they're out there, especially working those 12 to 16 hour shifts," Borell said. "So, at times, you won't see them, but just keep in mind, they are making their rounds, they might be getting fuel, salt, taking a break, but they're out there on the roads working hard to do their job."
